$comment: Operator decision log (scripts/analysis/decision-log.mjs; Spec 124 R-HK). Imported verbatim from the committed chat record docs/reports/decisions/raw/2026-10-22-page-eve/2026-10-22-page-eve.json. `decision_vocab`, `routing` (the register and row that record each decision), `amendments` and `options` are added by the lane and are not the operator's text; everything else is re-derived from `source.raw` by `--check`.

source.operator_quote: 62 cards answered. I just want to ensure that McBylaws will not use code - be standardized and fully observable - 3 layers, I want to make sure it is understandable and of course accurate.  We do want to keep it simple as possible.  Complexity will kill accuracy or trust. / spagetti code typo
source.record: operator Evening Rulings page (https://claude.ai/artifact/6ypnNKE5dkjkAV4HbPuokq), db collection decisions, exported 2026-10-22

decisions.question: Street names that contain a building-type word
decisions.recommendation: Yes: a type word immediately followed by a street suffix (Ave./St./Rd./Blvd.) is not a named type. — Yes. Narrow namedTypes() in scripts/analysis/bylaw/clause.mjs:112. No keyed unit changes; 767 (C) then passes; no other agreed unit has a street name with a type word.

decisions.question: 853 (B)(iii): how the clause is cited
decisions.recommendation: Keyer B (full path)

decisions.question: 1429 (A): building-history clause
decisions.recommendation: Keyer B (REQUIRE)

decisions.question: 478 (C): height limit for a detached house
decisions.recommendation: Keyer A (detached house only)

decisions.question: Exceptions 40, 863, 225: add a supplement?
decisions.recommendation: No: leave them below the floor. — No — keep to the census floor (no scope growth).

decisions.question: Six literal corrections by the lane
decisions.recommendation: Approve all six

decisions.question: 63 Johnston Ave: one parcel row, really two lots
decisions.recommendation: Scoped DATA flag now; report the two-lots-in-one-row defect to the parcel source; remove the flag when fixed. — Scoped DATA flag now, and fix the parcel row at the source; the flag goes when the data is fixed.

decisions.question: A round that exposes older wrong answers
decisions.recommendation: Hold the 478 shard; land the rest; re-check 10.5.60 after the merge. — Hold 478 and land the rest: no floor is waived, and the openings field can be its own ruling later.

decisions.question: Garden-suite side yard: use the window evidence
decisions.recommendation: Leave the DIFFER; extract independent window evidence later. — Leave it: a scorer must not read the answer to produce the answer.

decisions.question: Licence pattern: "one dwelling unit"
decisions.recommendation: Yes: add the pattern; 324 (C) becomes a LIMIT. — Yes: matches the existing single-count limits; pattern growth by ruling.

decisions.question: Licence pattern: "front lot line that abuts a street"
decisions.recommendation: Yes: add the pattern. — Yes.

decisions.question: 155 (A): units capped per registered-plan block
decisions.recommendation: UNUSUAL (disclosed). — UNUSUAL: the buyer should see the cap disclosed.

decisions.question: Twin variance: 1429 (A) vs 1436 (D)
decisions.recommendation: Match the 1436 (D) / CHAT-67.1434A form. — Match the 1436 (D) form you ruled in CHAT-67.

decisions.question: 958 (D)/(E): use permission tied to a 1978 date
decisions.recommendation: UNUSUAL on the rule-31 building-history route. — A: rule 31 says a permission that depends on a building-history date is never a target-less PERMIT.

decisions.question: "Despite (B)" pointing at a sibling clause
decisions.recommendation: subordinate_reference (existing). — Use the existing reason; nothing new to rule.

decisions.question: Round 8: approve the applied readings
decisions.recommendation: Approve as applied. — Approve, after verify-40 reports (I will flag anything it disputes here).

decisions.question: Licence pattern: "minimum frontage"
decisions.recommendation: Yes: add the pattern. — Yes.

decisions.question: Licence pattern: "from a front line"
decisions.recommendation: Yes: add the pattern. — Yes. (Suggest one pattern-growth ruling covering R6-1, R6-2, R8-5 and R9-1 together.)

decisions.question: Garage and ancillary setbacks: which target
decisions.recommendation: The named yard decides the target. — The named yard decides: matches the 26 resolved units and the vocabulary definitions.

decisions.question: Empty runs must still report every counter
decisions.recommendation: Keep it per step. — Per-materializer lock now; a fleet lock only by a later ruling.

decisions.question: The {sql} re-arm bracket as a #38 form
decisions.recommendation: Accept as an R-CZ #38 form. — Accept: it is already in use and verified in the runbook.

decisions.question: COA-D7 closed on a weaker lock
decisions.recommendation: Hold it back until execution.maintenance has a test. — Hold it back until execution.maintenance has a test.

decisions.question: Lineage snapshot still says link_coa stamps last_seen_at
decisions.recommendation: B: a reviewed one-line removal of last_seen_at from the snapshot row, citing R-JM; the next refresh converges. — B: smallest change, matches the code, heals itself on the next refresh.

decisions.question: Witness check and the UPDATE key column
decisions.recommendation: Exempt the key column(s) in the witness gate (gate script only, red fixture test; no lib/step change, no fleet recapture). — Exempt the key in the gate: the key is not written, so it should not be required in SET; no fleet impact.

decisions.question: Four tables, not five
decisions.recommendation: Approve the four-table design. — Approve as designed.

decisions.question: Results per building class
decisions.recommendation: Approve. — Approve as designed.

decisions.question: Map membership source
decisions.recommendation: Approve. — Approve as designed.

decisions.question: Scenario-axis check I13
decisions.recommendation: Approve WARN with a ceiling variable. — Approve as designed. The variable name is not set in the source.

decisions.question: permitted_by_class on the lot row
decisions.recommendation: Approve (+0.08 GB). — Approve as designed.

decisions.question: Disclosures stored once, not per cell
decisions.recommendation: Yes: a disclosure-set id; sentences stored once. — Yes: same idea as form C (store each distinct thing once); keeps Layer 2 inside the storage line.

decisions.question: Which tables I14 rechecks in SQL
decisions.recommendation: All four tables. — All four: a wrong signature, profile or lot row is as harmful as a wrong cell, and the canonical text is already defined for each.

decisions.question: Zone population: one list variable
decisions.recommendation: One list variable; add the config list arm in ①. — One list variable, landed on the planned fleet night (no extra recapture).

decisions.question: Layer 2 storage budget until first measurement
decisions.recommendation: 1,300 MB interim; re-set from the first POST measurement. — Yes: it sits just inside the measured room.

decisions.question: Run id on data rows
decisions.recommendation: Leave it empty (or drop the column). — Drop or leave empty: the run row already records it; follow the runner standard.

decisions.question: Unused Layer 2 rows after a by-law change
decisions.recommendation: Keep until reset; WARN with a count. — Keep until reset with a WARN count: simpler and observable.

decisions.question: Equivalence check instead of a time budget
decisions.recommendation: Yes: equivalence sample; run time measured by the runner. — Yes: it checks correctness, and the runner already times the run.

decisions.question: Layer 2 may not fit the storage line
decisions.recommendation: Intern the repeated payloads; re-measure. — Intern them: same idea as form C and Q-H, and it keeps Layer 2 inside the line you approved.

decisions.question: R-EMIT: a fixture for every reason code?
decisions.recommendation: Yes: add the fixture clause as its own row. — Yes, as a separate row: it proves each code can actually happen, which the static check cannot.

decisions.question: R-DET: also lock the shared library?
decisions.recommendation: Yes: widen the lock to the library. — Yes: the library computes the hashed keys, so it needs the same guarantee.

decisions.question: Name of the list-type logic variable
decisions.recommendation: Ratify "list" as built. — Ratify as built: it mirrors the string type and adds nothing else.

decisions.question: Drop old backup tables
decisions.recommendation: Yes: drop them. — Yes. The source gives the size and names only; nothing else is claimed.

decisions.question: Closed list of not-applicable reasons
decisions.recommendation: Yes: add the list by register row. — Yes, by register row.

decisions.question: No CoA u-factors seeded now
decisions.recommendation: Confirm: seed none; absent reads as unfitted. — Confirm.

decisions.question: Fleet recapture night for the intake
decisions.recommendation: Yes: land it with one fleet recapture night (plus migration 284 and the first ingest). — Yes: one library path per source form is the standard (Spec 132 §ingestor.3); a recapture night is the established way to land a library change.

decisions.question: Two new columns
decisions.recommendation: Yes: add both. — Yes.

decisions.question: Wider closed value lists
decisions.recommendation: Yes. — Yes: each value records a fact the source really lacks; nothing is guessed.

decisions.question: Plan facts: a new table?
decisions.recommendation: Yes: a new values-only table. — Yes: same form, values only, sha-pinned; you said these files are valuable beyond the scorer.

decisions.question: Batch pair-rate floor
decisions.recommendation: Report only until two more batches exist. — Report only until two more batches exist: three points are too few to set a floor.

decisions.question: The other CoA document types in Drive
decisions.recommendation: Not now: list them and revisit. — Not now: record them in the manifest; design a schema when a consumer (Phase 3 or the report) names a field it needs. This keeps scope to named uses (CHAT-68.scope).

decisions.question: 59 Yarrow Rd notice missing
decisions.recommendation: Leave it excluded.

decisions.question: Main-building geometry model (attic, dormers)
decisions.recommendation: Use the golden cases (keying page) as the check: key a few attic/dormer cases first. — Check it against your golden cases: real plans are the honest oracle; the model then gets ruled from evidence.

decisions.question: Maximum bedrooms
decisions.recommendation: Layer 3 applies the P5.4 per-unit rule to the Layer 2 inputs. — Layer 3 applies the P5.4 rule: no new Layer 2 axis, smallest change.

decisions.question: RD flat-roof wall height 7.2 m
decisions.recommendation: Yes: add the target by pin change. — Yes: every by-law number lives in the table, not in code.

decisions.question: RULED rows and the floor-change door
decisions.recommendation: Accept RULED as authority (change the reader). — Accept RULED in the reader: the operator approval is the authority; one reader change instead of re-labelling rows.

decisions.question: Round runner reads oracle C v2
decisions.recommendation: Yes: amend M-115 to v1 and v2. — Yes: it records what the code does.

decisions.question: Go for the fleet recapture night
decisions.recommendation: Go, as soon as integrate-25 is pushed. — Go after integrate-25 is pushed; I start it, watch it, and report numbers against the expected figures.

decisions.question: Houseplex lift zones (R, RT, RM)
decisions.recommendation: Layer 2 target. — Layer 2 target: the law lives in the table.

decisions.question: Minimum houseplex unit count (2)
decisions.recommendation: Pinned logic variable houseplex_min_units = 2. — Pinned logic variable: visible and adjustable in admin, cited to the houseplex definition.

decisions.question: Trust level for not-permitted rows
decisions.recommendation: Give them their own level (e.g. n/a). — Own level (n/a): "high" with zero checks would overstate confidence.

decisions.question: Shadow gate also blocks on Layer 2 defects
decisions.recommendation: Yes: gate on all three. — Yes: a known Layer 2 defect should not pass silently.

decisions.question: When the hidden-number check starts blocking
decisions.recommendation: Blocking at Phase 3 close, in step-validate. — Blocking at Phase 3 close: SC-6 says 0 open hidden constants at Phase 3 close.

decisions.question: Six non-law constants
decisions.recommendation: Yes: register as model_heuristic. — Yes: every constant is either a law number (sourced) or a declared heuristic.

decisions.question: Tolerances for the golden-case comparison
decisions.recommendation: Rule them with the calculation floors. — With the calculation floors: they should come from measured golden cases.

decisions.question: Settings for the Phase 3 step ① draft
decisions.recommendation: Accept all six as recommended. — Accept as recommended; each follows the existing step pattern (Spec 132 §x-stages.1/.2).

decisions.question: Settings in the Phase 3 compute module
decisions.recommendation: Accept the interim settings. — Accept: each is marked and replaced when its producer or ruling lands.

decisions.question: Main-wall shares where height is not regulated
decisions.recommendation: Code only: shares read only when a height limit exists. — Code only: a share of a wall height that is not limited has no meaning; no new absence entries needed.

decisions.question: RM townhouse and semi-detached houseplex: main-wall height
decisions.recommendation: Extend ABS-7.3 to the two types (four absent phrases added, expert sample kept). — Extend it: the clause text names only detached and semi-detached houses; with Q-KG1 the rows then compute with the main-wall limit equal to the height.

decisions.question: Absence when a conditional clause does not apply
decisions.recommendation: Yes: rule 7a ignores a clause whose lot condition is known false; then add the family absence entries. — Yes, once for the family (R, RT, RM townhouse length): the text sets no limit there.
